decisions.reason: The hook-training example does not restrict or otherwise change which source videos may be selected.
Mastering the new approach is a prerequisite for future Lead Clipper advancement, not a change to the current initial clipper qualification process.
The source explicitly permits new shorter clip styles. The existing same-message AMBIGUOUS Event captures uncertainty about the prior numeric limits but omits this concrete new permission.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey team,

First, sorry for the delay lately. Upwork had us on hold and we couldn't move as fast as we wanted. That's sorted now, so we're back to full speed.

While we were on hold, I put together a new system to make your job easier and help you hit your 100 approved clips faster.

Here's what's new:

1\. Clip variations - you can now take the same body clip and change just the hook/opening to make a new version. You can reuse one clip up to 2-3 times this way. Less work, more clips.

2\. Shorter clip styles - these are quicker to make and easier to combine, so reaching 100 approved clips will be a lot smoother. Some of you could even push past 200 if you want.

3\. Hook training video - I'm making a video showing you how to find strong hooks. One long video can give you close to 50 clip ideas. This will make finding content faster and easier.

We see the work, loyalty, and commitment you've all put in, even with the delays on our end, and we appreciate it. This new system is to help you earn more without extra headaches.

Looking ahead, we want to build you up into Lead Clippers as we grow and bring more people onto the team. That starts with mastering this new approach.

More details and examples coming soon. Let's get back to it.

\- Cleavon

decisions.reason: The source establishes that hook variations count as new clip versions intended to help reach the 100-approved-clip target. The existing RESUME Event does not capture this new quota-production rule.

value_updates.variation_counting_rule: Changing the hook/opening creates a new clip version, and the same body clip may be reused up to 2-3 times toward approved-clip production.

decisions.reason: Training on hook selection does not change the existing requirement to select strong source moments.
The new clip-production methods do not change which clips may be published, the publishing destination, or the publication format.
Clip variations and shorter styles remain subject to the existing client-approval gate; the source does not change approval authority or rejected-clip handling.
Permitting shorter styles does not necessarily permit fragments or revoke the requirement that each clip deliver a complete standalone lesson.
Changing hooks and permitting shorter clip styles does not alter caption color, font, effects, lettering, or position.
The new production approach does not change the clean, simple editing standard or the restrictions on effects and transitions.
The source changes clip creation methods but says nothing about submission channels, folder naming, access, or review-link delivery.
The source does not change the requirement to remove distracting wind noise.
